description: A pipeline: tasks with dependencies and an optional schedule, run on one engine.

spec.description: A pipeline: tasks with dependencies, an optional schedule, run by one engine.

concurrency.description: What happens when a run is due while the previous one is still running.

engine.description: Engine that orchestrates (and for `spark`, executes) the pipeline.

ownerGroup.description:
The group that owns the pipeline: its members see it, run it and pause it in Nova. Optional so
that existing pipelines keep working; a pipeline without an owner is visible to administrators only.

publish.description:
`direct` (default) or `wap`; `wap` needs a `quality` task with at least one check
(nova#628 decision 1).

retries.description: Retry policy applied to every task.

attempts.description: Extra attempts after the first failure.

backoff.description: Wait between attempts, for example `5m`. Absent means one minute.

runAs.description:
Service principal the tasks run as. Absent means the platform's default pipeline principal.
By convention the principal of the owner group, named `pipeline-<ownerGroup>`; Nova's Schedule
writes that name.

schedule.description: Optional schedule; a pipeline without one runs on demand only.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Absent means UTC.

tasks.description: Tasks of the pipeline; at least one, at most 30.

items.description:
One task of a `Pipeline`. A task starts when every task in `dependsOn` has succeeded.

A `notebook` task names its source in `config`: `notebook` is the `.ipynb`
file name and `objectVersion` the immutable published version; `params` is a
JSON object string that papermill passes to the notebook. Nothing else is
accepted, so a typo cannot silently become a default.

checks.description: A `quality` task's assertions; empty on every other kind.

items.description: One SQL assertion of a `quality` task: the check passes when the query returns no rows.

name.description: Unique within the task; the run page names the check by it.

severity.description: `error` fails the run; `warn` records the rows and lets the run publish.

sql.description:
The assertion; it passes when it returns zero rows. `${table}` is the branch-qualified
table during the audit (nova#628 decision 2).

config.description: Task-specific parameters of the other kinds (model path, gate threshold, …).

connection.description:
The `Connection` whose secret fields this task receives as `CONN_<NAME>_<KEY>`: the name
upper-cased with `-` written as `_`. The credentials reach the pod through `secretKeyRef`s
and are never part of the resource, the DAG or a log. A `sql` task runs inside the engine
and cannot name one.

dependsOn.description: Names of the tasks that must succeed first.

kind.description:
What a pipeline task does — the task contract behind `Pipeline`
(master spec §5, plugs 6, 7 and 12). `sql` and `notebook` run today
(scheduled jobs phases J0 and J1); `python`, `dbt` and `quality` are
accepted so manifests can be written ahead of their runtimes.

name.description: Unique within the pipeline; becomes the task id in the engine.

sql.description:
The statement of a `sql` task. `${run.date}`, `${run.id}` and
`${params.<name>}` are expanded when the task runs, not in the resource.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs a `sql` task; absent means the default warehouse.

writes.description:
The tables a `sql` task writes, as `catalog.schema.table`. Only these get an audit
branch when `spec.publish: wap`; a read leaves them alone (nova#628 decision 3).

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a notebook task needs config.notebook (a .ipynb file name) and config.objectVersion (the published version)
notebook tasks accept only notebook, objectVersion and params
notebook params must be a JSON object string of at most 4096 characters
a sql task cannot name a connection: it runs inside the engine
only a sql task declares writes
only a quality task declares checks

timeout.description: Longest a whole run may take, for example `2h`.

viewers.description:
Groups that may READ the pipeline in Nova — list it, open it, see its runs — and
nothing else. Running, pausing, resuming and deleting stay with `ownerGroup`.
Absent means the owner group only, which is what every pipeline had before this field.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: dependsOn must name other tasks of this pipeline
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: self.tasks.all(t, !has(t.dependsOn) || t.dependsOn.all(d, d != t.name && self.tasks.exists(u, u.name == d)))

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a sql task needs a sql statement
publish: wap needs a quality task with at least one check
publish: wap needs a task that writes at least one table

items.description:
Last-known run of a pipeline. Intentionally minimal: the authoritative history
belongs to the engine adapter (Airflow / Spark); this is the operator's view.
